text:
maria_support: FYI customer 'VeloxFinance' reporting 504s and intermittent 5xx from hosted API since ~08:10 UTC. They see long waits then an immediate 504. Attaching their request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d
cheng_oncall: seeing correlated spike in request_queue_depth for hosted-west-1 around that time. p95 latency jumped from 120ms to 2.3s, p99 to ~12s. Queues show continuous-batcher backlog growing.
anna_cs: customer says it started after a marketing send - large burst of small chat completions. They say payloads are small (<= 200 tokens) but high concurrency from many users. Billing spikes might be from retries.
oliver_infra: snapshot of queue metrics (08:09-08:18):
```
queue_depth:  1k -> 12k
active_batchers: 24 -> 18
avg_batch_size: 6 -> 28
batch_window_ms: 25
max_queue_depth_configured: 5000
early_reject_count: 0
```
oliver_infra: notable: max_queue_depth was set to 5000 for hosted pool; we hit >12k so we were dropping into an unhandled backlog leading to huge tail latencies and gateway timeouts.
sre-alerts: alert: continuous-batching-backlog > threshold -> created incident 2210004321
maria_support: customer repro steps:
- POST /v1/chat/completions with model=redwood-alpha-small
- 250 concurrent connections (websocket/short polling), each sending 4 reqs/s for ~3 min
- many retries at client side when timeout
cheng_oncall: looks like two factors: our batcher auto-sizes batch size up when longer queues to improve throughput which raises per-request latency for tail requests; and max_queue_depth was misaligned with tenant burst throttles. Also notice early_reject_count==0 because early-reject was disabled for this pool.
anna_cs: customer asks why this wasn't automatically shed earlier.
oliver_infra: we had an override in the config from last month to disable early rejects for lower error noise. Bad timing.
maria_support: immediate mitigation options?
cheng_oncall: short term:
- re-enable early_rejects for hosted-west-1 (threshold 6000 -> start rejecting beyond 6k) to avoid unbounded backlog
- scale up batchers pool + spin a temporary dedicated pool for the tenant (if they authorize) - but that takes ~5-7 min
- enable model-fallback to smaller variant for hosted tier to reduce per-token compute
oliver_infra: I'm reapplying early_reject policy now via infra-runbook command:
```
infractl set-pool-config --region hosted-west-1 --pool shared --max-queue-depth 6000 --enable-early-reject true
```
deploy-bot: apply started (run-id: apply-2210004321-01) — ETA ~30s
deploy-bot: apply finished: success
cheng_oncall: early_rejects now on. watching queue.
sre-alerts: queue_depth dropped from 12k -> 4.2k over 90s after early rejects and client backoff. p95 dropped to 180ms, p99 to ~2.1s.
maria_support: relaying to customer and asking them to throttle retries/backoff. also requested their client-side request-ids for a few examples.
anna_cs: customer provided sample trace: rq_0a1b2c3d has server-side latency 11.6s and then gateway 504. They confirmed they had exponential backoff at 3s which was too aggressive.
cheng_oncall: long term fixes we discussed in-thread:
- add tenant burst protections that are token-aware not just request-count aware
- make early_reject default for shared pools and ensure not toggled off during maintenance
- autoscale batchers faster based on queue depth deltas and not just CPU
- implement a graceful degrade path: when queue depth crosses X, switch some traffic to a cold-model with lower compute or cached responses
oliver_infra: action items assigned:
- @cheng_oncall: draft change to default early_reject policy and add canary test (ETA 2d)
- @oliver_infra: add faster autoscale rule (ETA 3d)
- @maria_support / @anna_cs: follow up with customer for post-incident questionnaire and compensation if needed
- @eng-runtime (not on thread): evaluate smaller-quantized model variants for fallback (RFC)
maria_support: customer verified recovery and reduced retry rate; they still saw a handful of 504s during the window but acceptance of mitigation. They asked for suggested SDK retry settings.
cheng_oncall: recommend SDK backoff: initial 250ms jittered, max backoff 3s, max retries 4 for non-idempotent chat. Also send request-id with every retry to help de-dupe.
anna_cs: logging this as a Sev3. tagging for postmortem. please include dashboard graphs: queue_depth, p95/p99 latency, batch_size, early_rejects, pool_count.
maria_support: thanks team. Will keep this thread updated with CS notes and postmortem link when ready. :thumbsup:
cheng_oncall: closing incident once postmortem published and config change merged.
